# NPM Improved v1.6.15 — October 2026 Node.js Security Update

## Important: update installed NPM Improved instances

This security release updates **the actual Node.js application executable** used by the NPM Improved management API to **Node.js 24.22.1**. The Node.js project shipped this release on October 21, 2026 to correct vulnerabilities including DNS hostname parsing and TLS certificate hostname verification.

NPMi v1.6.14 successfully patched the public-facing NGINX proxy engine, but its application image inherited an older Node.js runtime from the v1.4.0 container. NGINX version checks alone cannot establish the Node.js patch status. This update adds an explicit patched Node.js runtime to the image.

## Security changes

- Replace the inherited Node.js runtime executable with the official **Node.js 24.22.1** release.
- Verify the **executing Node.js version inside the built Docker image**; fail the build/security gate if the runtime is not 24.22.1.
- Preserve the prior **NGINX 1.31.8** and matching HTTP/stream GeoIP2 module security checks.
- Preserve existing management API, database migrations, proxy hosts, certificates, NPMX pairing/synchronization, user permissions, and the updater/rollback workflow.
- No intentional feature removal or routing configuration changes.

## Upgrade guidance

1. Back up your NPM Improved data and Let's Encrypt volumes before deployment.
2. Use **Settings → Update** after v1.6.15 is published and the correct architecture build is available. **Update NPMX primary and secondary sequentially**, verifying both nodes return to the same version.
3. Confirm live versions using `docker exec CONTAINER node -v` (expect `v24.22.1`) and `docker exec CONTAINER nginx -v` (expect `nginx/1.31.8`).
4. Validate management login, important HTTPS proxy hosts, certificates and NPMX last successful sync/heartbeat.
5. This change only protects **running containers rebuilt and restarted** into the v1.6.15 image; existing v1.6.14 installations are not automatically updated by merging source.
